name: Petapa Zapotec
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are wordlists/sociolinguistics only (Pena Godinez 2019 heritage-language thesis; Brueske 1976 ethnography; Smith Stark 1994 wordlist); no grammar or phonology of Petapa Zapotec located.

sources.citation: Peña Godínez, Amairani del Rosario. 2022. La revitalización lingüística del zapoteco de Santo Domingo Petapa, Oaxaca: el desarrollo de métodos colaborativos con una comunidad de práctica. Tesis de maestría en Antropología Social, CIESAS Sureste. 206 pp. (repositorio CIESAS handle 1015/1555, open access CC BY-NC-SA)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: First-approximation phonology of 'zapoteco domingano' (Santo Domingo Petapa), pp. 137-139: six vowels (a e i o u æ), level and contour tones (alto, bajo, ascendente, descendente), three glottalized vowel types citing Benn 2021, consonant table. Only stress remark is anecdotal (p. 139 + fn. 163): one word [nà.ʃì.ˈjé] naxiyé 'oloroso' where speakers asked whether the last syllable 'llevaba acento' and chose to mark accent rather than tone; footnote asks whether stress is replacing tone in heritage speakers. No statement of where word stress falls. Appendix (pp. 183 ff.) reproduces a 2004 phonem…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and reference records for peta1247 (Hammarström et al.), incl. Glottolog's most extensive descriptions and subclassification comments; hh.bib held by the project
sources.note: No descriptive source: Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are Peña Godinez 2019 (socling), Smith Stark 1994 (overview), Brueske 1976 (ethnographic), all 'a wordlist or less'. Subclassification comments cite Benn 2016 (ref 586097) and Benn 2021 (ref 671933, phonology;comparative, coded to zpg).

sources.citation: Benn, Joshua. 2016. Consonant-Tone-Phonation Interactions in Guienagati Zapotec. Proc. 5th International Symposium on Tonal Aspects of Languages (TAL 2016), Buffalo, pp. 125-128. doi:10.21437/TAL.2016-27
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology of Guienagati [zpg] with Petapa Zapotec cognate forms (Tables 1, 4-5: CVCV roots retained in Petapa, contrastive breathiness, rearticulated vowels, tones). Nothing on stress/accent for Petapa or Guienagati; Petapa data credited to the Sicoli & Kaufman Zapotec-Chatino Survey Archive (restricted).

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed., entry 'Zapotec, Petapa' [zpe] (the Internet Archive capture, 2016)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 8,000 speakers (1990), Santa María Petapa and Santo Domingo Petapa; 55% intelligibility of Guevea [zpg], 34% of Lachiguiri [zpa]; 'Unwritten'.

sources.citation: Benn, Joshua. 2021. The phonetics, phonology, and historical development of Guienagati Zapotec. PhD dissertation, State University of New York at Buffalo. 236 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login
sources.note: The only modern phonological description that includes first-hand Petapa Zapotec data (Peña Godínez 2022 fn. 161: Benn did fieldwork in Santo Domingo Petapa and calls the variety 'zapoteco de Petapa'); a phonetics/phonology dissertation on the sister language Guienagati with comparative NETZ chapters is the most likely place for an explicit stress statement covering Petapa. Glottolog ref 671933 (phonology;comparative).

sources.note: Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description for peta1247 (sociolinguistic); may contain a preliminary linguistic sketch of Santa María/Santo Domingo Petapa Zapotec; a PDF exists in Hammarström's collection but was not located online.
